newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Former Zimbabwe president faces sodomy charges.
newsitem.headline: Former Zimbabwe president faces sodomy charges.

text.p: Former Zimbabwe state president Canaan Banana will soon be charged with 11 counts of sodomy, attempted sodomy and indecent assault, Attorney-General Patrick Chinamasa said on Thursday.

Chinamasa said in a statement that Banana -- who has been under police investigation since February after allegations that he had raped and forced one of his former aides-de-camp into a homosexual relationship in the 1980s -- would be brought to court within the next few days.
The former aide, Jefta Dube, was sentenced in February to 10 years in jail for the 1995 fatal shooting of a fellow policeman who goaded him by calling him "Banana's wife".
Dube told the court then that his homosexual subjugation by Banana had made him depressive and an alcoholic, and judge David Bartlett ruled that Dube had diminished responsibility.
The judge ordered the police to investigate Dube's charges against Banana, saying they were "probably true".

Banana, a 61-year-old Methodist priest who is married and has four children, has dismissed Dube's accusation and any suggestions that he is a homosexual as "a mortuary of pathological lies and a malicious vendetta of vilification and character assassination".

But on Thursday, the attorney-general said Banana -- who served as a largely ceremonial president for seven years up to 1987 when then prime minister Robert Mugabe became an executive president -- had a case to answer.
Homosexuality and sodomy are illegal in Zimbabwe and individual cases carry jail terms of up to 10 years.
Chinamasa said Banana's trial will be held in an open court, but for the protection of witnesses' reputations, their names and particulars of their identities may not be made public.
He said he expected the trial to last at least three weeks.
